reason: The flora says the stamens are inserted on an androphore. That is the bearer stamen, the quality 'inserted into' (PATO_0000624), and the target androphore.
The capsule is called oblong-cylindric, so 'cylindrical' on the fruit is true. 'Oblong' only refines the outline.
The blade is hirtellous on the underside, along the veins. Saying the abaxial surface is hairy is true; 'along veins' only narrows where the hairs are.
A densely many-flowered inflorescence: flowers present inside the inflorescence, with the count 'many', is right.
The underside is glabrescent on the veins. This is true at the level of the abaxial surface. 'Sometimes' means it varies; it does not deny the statement.
The pod is canescent when young. The context quality PATO_0000309 is 'young', so the stage is recorded.
'Feuilles: 6–8' gives a count of 6 to 8 leaves.

fix: A hyphenated compound shape (e.g. 'linear-elliptic') names one in-between shape; it is not a range from 'linear' to 'elliptic'. The range is the 'to' between the two compounds. The hyphen inside a compound should not be read as a range connector.
reason: The relation was read inside the first compound (linear to elliptic). The flora's range is linear-elliptic to linear-oblong.
'Sépales et pétales ... 2–3 mm de large' covers the petals too, so a petal width of 2–3 mm is right.

fix: 'Glaucous' means covered with a bluish-white waxy bloom. Map it to PATO glaucous, not to 'approximately green'.
reason: The flora says the leaf blades are glaucous. That is not 'approximately green'.
The inflorescence is 4.5 cm in diameter.
Stamens shorter than petals: decreased length of the stamen, compared with the petal.
The petals are white or purple, given as alternatives.

The blade margins are entire, dentate or pinnatisect. PATO 'entire' has the synonym 'entire margin', and pinnatisect is a dissection of the blade, so the leaf lamina is an acceptable bearer. Leaf lamina margin (PO_0025009) would be more exact for entire and dentate.

fix: A compound shape 'ovate-oblong' is one in-between shape. Splitting it into the separate alternatives 'oblong' and 'ovate' claims a plain oblong blade, which the flora does not say.
reason: The alternatives are ovate-oblong or long-ovate. 'Oblong' on its own is not stated.
Two leaves per node, with the node as the position landmark.
'Abaxially glabrous' means the underside of the blade is glabrous.
Two secondary veins on each side of the midvein (PO_0020139), inside the blade.

fix: 'X bristle-tipped' means the apex of X ends in a bristle. The bristle has to be tied to X as its whole (or annotated as a bristle at the apex of X). Without that it reads as a free-standing awn on the plant.
reason: The bristle tips belong to the involucral bracts, and the annotation does not record that.

fix: An achene is a dry one-seeded fruit. Map 'achene' to a fruit class, never to seed.
reason: The flora says the achenes (fruits) are substipitate, not the seed.
'Perennial herb': the whole plant is herbaceous. 'Somewhat woody near the base' does not undo this.
'Thorns & Spines: Absent' means no thorns, so thorn absent is right. Spine absent is implied too.
The berry (fruit) is red.
The leaves range from erect to more or less spreading in position.
The style is longer than the ovary.
Homomallous (all leaves turned to one side) is essentially secund, so 'not secund' matches 'not homomallous'.
In FNA the size after 'Herbs' is the plant height. 2–5 dm becomes 20–50 cm, with the extremes 10 and 60 cm recorded. The taxon line shows the synonym Polygala leptocaulis, which is fine.
'Lacking ... wings' covers the wings, so the phyllaries (involucral bracts) are not winged.
'No scent' follows the flower description, so the flowers having no odour is the likely reading. It could be meant for the whole plant.
Triangular-lanceolate bracts match PATO 'lanceolate-triangular' (PATO_0002338).
